chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: The Town Hall evening: two shows and a mixed crowd
summary: They played two 45-minute shows including typical music, to a mixed crowd of Latins and Americans who danced Latin music.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: All right, we'll talk about that a little later when we get to '49. In that night, the first time you introduced Afro-Cuban jazz, January 24, 1947, at Town Hall, how long were you on stage?
Well, we did two forty-five minutes.
Did you have any special guest artists with you that night?
I don't remember, I think that we was alone.
Now, I know you were playing a lot of Afro-Cuban jazz tunes, did you do any tipica stuff?
Yeah, we did and the people accept it very well because a public is very, very curious. You give them something
they like and then they'll accept what you like. We always catered to the public because is the one to have the last word, but we tried out our thing and it was accepted.

Oh, yes, because - and there was a mixed crowd. You know, there was a latin, a lot of latin and a lot of American that know how to dance Latin music, Cuban music. So in those days there was the mambo and cha-cha-cha, conga and you name it, the whole business. So everybody went up there to hear us to play something new. The ones that was oriented by Cuban music, they went up there to see if we could do as good with the Afro-Cuban scene, So we had a combination, two crowds.
Okay. Now, being that you were accepted now as Afro-Cuban jazzmen, did you switch on and off, playing the tipica clubs and then the Afro-Cuban jazz thing wherever it called for it?
